rows.article: When you create or apply a rule

rows.label: TRIED, read AI alone (276g) · not proposed
rows.text: Limits like those come from two principles colliding, solidarity and each community's claim on its own labor and stores. Whenever you create or apply a rule where principles collide, don't only store the rule. Store the hard case too: what happened, the principles that actually conflicted, your first judgments, and your final decision and rationale. Any dissenting opinions should go in there as well, along with the consequences and which version of the rule it was decided under. When the rule changes, run the case through again. That saves each generation from having to rediscover the same constitutional fight from scratch.
